argument: Tested the leading support position that the 42 cards all land inside the flat damage budget; it breaks on stacking. The chapter itself rules that bonuses from different talents combine, and several effects each move a hit up one or more outcome tiers with no shared ceiling. Weapon Focus at Master adds three tiers to any ability card in its chosen weapon Discipline, Dangerous Gambit adds a fourth on a 12-or-higher roll twice per scene, and Power Strike or Charge each add one more. A Master-tier Strong result is already 21 and is the top row of the budget table, so even the two-talent core (Weapon Focus plus Dangerous Gambit, four tiers) has no row above it to land on, and adding a maneuver reaches roughly six tiers past the table. Broken value: stacked +N-tier riders push a hit off the printed budget. Expected: every result lands on a real row, or one global ceiling governs all tier bumps. The chapter shows it knows a cap is needed because Death Blow alone prints maximum 21, but that cap is applied to one card in 42. Same missing-limit gap has two more counter-examples: Combat Reflexes Master grants two extra Reactions yet silently drops the Adept tier's +1 Initiative, so Master is not a strict superset, and Riposte is a Reaction counterattack with no per-scene or per-round limit, so the extra Reactions convert directly into repeated full-damage counterattacks in a single round. Minimal fix: one rule that no result may rise above Strong for its card's rank, absolute maximum 21, applied to every tier-boost effect, plus usage lines on Reaction maneuvers.

evidence.claim: The chapter explicitly sanctions combining separate talents' bonuses, which is the stacking hook the overflow rides on.
Weapon Focus at Master adds three damage tiers to ability cards of one chosen weapon Discipline, uncapped and repeatable each attack.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +3 damage tiers on ability cards of the chosen weapon Discipline

evidence.claim: Dangerous Gambit raises the outcome one tier on a 14-plus roll, and its Master line does so twice per scene; this stacks with Weapon Focus.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: increase the damage tier of the result by one

evidence.claim: Power Strike is a weapon maneuver that moves the next weapon attack up one tier with no per-scene restriction, so it can feed the same boosted attack as the talents.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +1 damage tier on your next weapon attack

evidence.claim: Charge is a second tier bump a character can aim at the same pending attack on a later turn.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: make one attack at +1 damage tier

evidence.claim: Only Death Blow carries a ceiling; the omission of the same cap on every other tier booster is the defect.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: (one row up on the damage budget, maximum 21)

evidence.claim: Combat Reflexes Master grants two extra Reactions but silently drops the Adept tier's Initiative bonus, so the Master line is not a strict superset of Adept as passive cards require.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: You gain two extra Reactions per round

evidence.claim: The Adept line is the tier being superseded and it includes an Initiative bonus the Master line omits.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: one extra Reaction per round and +1 Initiative

evidence.claim: Riposte's Master tier counterattacks for the full Master row and prints no usage limit, so extra Reactions translate into repeated counterattacks within one round.
Renewal is the only weapon maneuver that prints an explicit usage cap, confirming the family has no consistent default limit.
